tagline: Nişantaşı's quieter, more refined neighbour — boutique shopping, excellent patisseries, and the kind of neighbourhood luxury that doesn't need to advertise.

items.name: Patisserie de Pera / Elit
items.description: Classic Istanbul patisseries in the Teşvikiye area serving exceptional pastries, cakes, and Turkish coffee. Old-school elegance.

items.name: Teşvikiye Cafés (Abdi İpekçi Cad.)
items.description: The luxury strip of Abdi İpekçi Caddesi has excellent café options with an upscale crowd — great for people-watching.

items.name: Abdi İpekçi Caddesi
items.description: Istanbul's luxury shopping street — Chanel, Gucci, Hermès, and all major international luxury brands. Turkey's Bond Street.

items.name: Teşvikiye Boutiques
items.description: The smaller streets off Abdi İpekçi have excellent Turkish designers and independent boutiques — often more interesting than the main strip.

items.name: Teşvikiye Camii
items.description: A beautiful 19th-century Ottoman baroque mosque — small, elegant, and often uncrowded. A peaceful counterpoint to the luxury shopping around it.

tips: Teşvikiye is the transition between Şişli (commercial) and Nişantaşı (luxury). Walk between them freely.
Osmanbey metro stop (M2) is the most convenient access point.
Better for boutique shopping than Nişantaşı proper — fewer tourists, same quality.
The side streets hide excellent lunch spots popular with local business people.
